recorded.prompt:q-pan-prefix: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pan-prefix: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pan-prefix: Section 13.3 works through this exact case: the host read `16`, took sixteen digits (eight bytes) as the PAN, began field 3 in the middle of the PAN, and nothing threw, which is option c.
recorded.prompt:q-track2-filler: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track2-filler: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track2-filler: Section 13.4 says a track 2 with an even number of characters has no filler and works, while one with an odd number gets the filler in front and is misread, which is option b.
recorded.prompt:q-config-path: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-config-path: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-config-path: Section 13.6.1 says that with `jar:` the name is a classpath resource and shows it loading from `/`, and it says the DTD comes from a copy inside the jPOS jar so loading works offline, which is option a.
recorded.prompt:q-which-row: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-which-row: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-which-row: Section 13.7's checklist says to find the first wrong value among the fields read, in field order, ignore the field the exception names, and check that field's row, which is option c.
recorded.prompt:q-chip-length: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-chip-length: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-chip-length: Section 13.3 shows `IFB_LLLBINARY(255), 300 bytes: packs 302 bytes`, says 'Three hundred bytes of chip data go out in a field limited to 255', and says pack checks the length only for fixed fields, which is option c.

gates.says: all 15 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-pan-prefix:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pan-prefix:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pan-prefix:a: Section 13.3 says both classes write `16` but IFB_LLNUM counts digits and IFB_LLCHAR counts bytes, and it shows the host reading the PAN as 3431313131313131, so the PAN is not read as sent.
recorded.prompt:q-pan-prefix:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pan-prefix:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pan-prefix:b: Section 13.3 shows the host's PAN as the raw ASCII bytes 3431313131313131 rather than the digits sent, and 13.9 says no field packager on the page checks content, so no conversion rescues the PAN.
recorded.prompt:q-pan-prefix:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pan-prefix:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pan-prefix:d: Section 13.3 says the host's IFB_LLNUM prefix counts digits, that 'Nothing threw', and that unpack returned 39 of 47, which refutes both the error and the reason given.
recorded.prompt:q-track2-filler:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track2-filler:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track2-filler:a: Section 13.4 says an even-length track 2 has no filler, and its 24-character example card is read correctly by the host.
recorded.prompt:q-track2-filler:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track2-filler:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track2-filler:c: Section 13.4 places the filler at the front or end of the whole field and makes it depend on the track 2's total length, so a short inference rules out a filler placed right after the PAN or decided by the PAN's own digit count.
recorded.prompt:q-track2-filler:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track2-filler:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track2-filler:d: Section 13.4's two example cards both have 16-digit (even) PANs, yet the host reads the 24-character track correctly, so an even PAN does not cause the misread.
recorded.prompt:q-config-path:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-config-path:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-config-path:b: Section 13.6.1 says that with the `jar:` prefix the rest of the name is a classpath resource, which by short inference rules out lookup in Q2's deploy directory, although the page never mentions a deploy directory.
recorded.prompt:q-config-path:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-config-path:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-config-path:c: Section 13.6.1 says only a name without `jar:` is a file path relative to the start directory, and its output shows the `jar:` name loading from `/`.
recorded.prompt:q-config-path:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-config-path:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-config-path:d: Section 13.6.1 says the DTD's http address is never fetched because jPOS resolves it to a copy inside its own jar, so loading works offline.
recorded.prompt:q-which-row:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-which-row:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-which-row:a: Section 13.7 says the field the exception names 'is usually fine' and tells the reader to ignore it.
recorded.prompt:q-which-row:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-which-row:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-which-row:b: In Section 13.7's example the last field read before the failure (41) is wrong only because it was shifted, and the page says the fault is the first field with a wrong value (11), so the last field read is not the one to check.
recorded.prompt:q-which-row:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-which-row:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-which-row:d: Section 13.7 says to choose the first wrong value in field order, and in its example field 41 (91100013 against 29110001) is further off than the faulty field 11 (000012), so the size of a difference is not the guide.
recorded.prompt:q-chip-length:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-chip-length:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-chip-length:a: Section 13.3 (and 13.9) says variable binary field packagers don't refuse a value over their length and shows 300 bytes packing without error.
recorded.prompt:q-chip-length:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-chip-length:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-chip-length:b: Section 13.3's run packed 302 bytes (300 plus the prefix) with no exception, so the prefix had room for 300.
recorded.prompt:q-chip-length:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-chip-length:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-chip-length:d: Section 13.3 says the three hundred bytes go out and shows 302 bytes packed, which is the full 300 plus the prefix rather than a value cut down to 255.
